subject: Guardian Health - Private Deploy: data lockdown & onboarding credit request
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@guardianhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Steven Park <steven.park@guardianhealth.com>, procurement@guardianhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment pilot — residency + audit scope + pricing request

Kimberly,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. Guardian is interested in a 6-month pilot of Redwood Private (VPC deployment) for our clinical NLP pipeline, but we have a few mandatory constraints to move forward:

- Data residency: instance must be provisioned in AWS us-east-1 and all backups must remain in our customer-managed S3 with keys we control.
- Audit access: Guardian legal requires monthly read-only forensic export snapshots (redacted PII allowed) for internal compliance reviews, with 14 days' notice. No live remote shell or ephemeral root access by vendor engineers.
- Deployment constraints: no inbound exec (SSH/RDP) from vendor; agent-based telemetry is acceptable if we can audit logs.

Given this, procurement is also asking for a pilot onboarding credit to offset integration effort and the additional engineering work we expect from Redwood. We're looking for a one-time onboarding credit and a fixed price for the 6-month pilot.

Attached is our security profile and an initial list of questions from Guardian InfoSec. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the limited audit export (read-only monthly) in lieu of live audit access, and whether you can offer a pilot credit?

Elena
Elena Morales
Director, Platform Partnerships
Guardian Health
(415) 555-0148
Attachment: Guardian_Security_Profile.pdf
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@guardianhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pilot — residency + audit scope + pricing request

Elena — thanks for the clear checklist and the profile. We can support provisioning in us-east-1 and customer-managed S3/KMS (bring-your-own-key) for snapshots.

Short answers up front:
- Read-only monthly forensic exports: feasible, with a defined process and 14 days' notice.
- No remote exec access from Redwood engineers: we can agree to that condition; we'll use an auditor-supervised export workflow for the snapshots.
- Telemetry: we can offer agent telemetry limited to operational metrics; full packet traces would require an exception.

On the pricing/credit side, I'll need to pull Deal Desk and legal in — copying Karthik and Rishi. My ask: Deal Desk to evaluate a one-time onboarding credit for the pilot and confirm whether the audit carveouts are acceptable risk-wise.

I'll follow up with a formal summary and an internal risk note.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_internal_risk_note.txt
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Guardian — Deal Desk evaluation request (audit scope + credit)

Team — quick assessment before we escalate:

1) Risk summary: Guardian's ask (no live remote exec, monthly read-only exports with 14 days' notice, BYOK for backups) materially reduces our typical audit process. That lowers our ability to troubleshoot incidents and increases operational overhead for the first 90 days. However, the account is strategically important (large hospital system) and could convert to Dedicated reserved capacity.

2) Proposed commercial concessions for pilot: 15% one-time onboarding credit applied to first invoice OR a fixed $35k onboarding credit (whichever Kimberly prefers). We should treat this as a pilot concession with a 3-month tech review gate.

3) Legal carveouts recommended:
- Audit: accept scheduled, read-only export only; require Guardian to execute a security addendum that prohibits re-sharing raw exports and defines redaction requirements.
- Access: no live exec access; vendor must provide a technician-read-only shadow session for troubleshooting if invited by Guardian.

4) Operational mitigations: product must sign off that monthly snapshot exports are supported without data integrity risk and that we can produce full telemetry for the first 30 days for incident triage (kept in our logs for 90 days).

Please escalate to Deal Desk / Execs: we need approval to: (A) grant the onboarding credit, (B) accept the audit/export-only approach with a legal addendum, and (C) lock the no-remote-exec clause for the pilot.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal (Contracts) — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Guardian — request for exec signoff (onboarding credit + audit carveout)

Vivek / Marissa — forwarding for exec review.

Summary of ask: Guardian Health requires a VPC in us-east-1 with BYOK backups, monthly read-only export snapshots (14-day notice), and no live vendor exec access. They want a pilot onboarding credit to offset integration. Karthik recommends a pilot concession (15% or $35k) with a 3-month review and a security addendum to prohibit re-sharing of raw exports. Product/ops confirm export process is safe.

Why escalate: this is a non-standard audit approach + commercial concession for a strategic account. Approve/deny the credit and carveout so I can get back to procurement and legal.

Kim

Date: 2026-10-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Guardian — request for exec signoff (onboarding credit + audit carveout)

Quick thoughts:

- I support a pilot concession but would prefer a percentage credit rather than a flat $ to keep alignment with consumption. Recommend 15% onboarding credit applied to first invoice.
- Approve the audit-export-only model for the pilot under strict legal controls: signed security addendum, explicit redaction rules, and penalties for re-sharing.
- Product ask: confirm that we can produce monthly read-only forensic exports in the requested format and that agent telemetry can be scoped down. Also require a 3-month technical gate to evaluate rollback to standard audit access if needed.

Operational addition: first 30 days we need enhanced on-call support (we assign a tech lead) — include as part of the concession.

If legal prepares the addendum and Deal Desk issues a one-time 15% credit, I'm comfortable approving the pilot.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product — Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@guardianhealth.com>, Steven Park <steven.park@guardianhealth.com>, procurement@guardianhealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pilot — residency + audit scope + pricing request

Elena / Steven — thanks for the patience while we evaluated this. Executive decision and next steps below: 

1) Commercial: Redwood will grant a one-time 15% onboarding credit applied to the first invoice of the 6-month pilot (Deal ID DEAL-7832). This is a pilot concession and will be reflected in the SOW.

2) Audit & access carveout: For the pilot only, Redwood will accept scheduled, read-only monthly forensic exports (14 days' notice) in lieu of live remote exec access. Guardian must sign a Security Addendum that: (a) prohibits re-sharing of raw exports, (b) defines acceptable redaction rules, and (c) allows Redwood to retain a copy of telemetry for 90 days for incident triage.

3) Operational support: Redwood will assign a technical lead for elevated support during the first 30 days. No vendor live shell access will be performed without explicit Guardian invitation.

4) Review gate: A technical review will occur at month 3 to evaluate whether the carveout remains acceptable or whether additional access must be granted for troubleshooting.

Legal will draft the Security Addendum and SOW with the approved concession; procurement, please confirm whether you prefer a percentage or flat-dollar credit reflected in the SOW (we will default to the 15% credit unless you ask for the $35k flat).

I will route the addendum to Steven for signature once it's ready. Looking forward to getting Guardian onboarded.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: approved_exceptions_signed.stamp.pdf
